tier_reason: The numbers come from a peer-reviewed paper (Castaneda Lozano, Carlsson, Hjort Blindell, Schulte, ACM TOPLAS 41(3) 2019, arXiv 1804.02452), but arXiv, doi.org and every mirror tried (deepai.org, the Ericsson research blog) were unreachable here, and the repo and project-site sources carry no results, so the figures are known only from search snippets. Held at C (snippet-only rule) pending a paper-access retier; it would be B once the paper is opened.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (arXiv 1804.02452 abstract via WebSearch; paper not opened): mean estimated speedup over LLVM from 1.1% to 10% and mean code size reduction from 1.3% to 3.8% depending on the architecture (code size: MIPS 3.8%, ARM 2.5%, Hexagon 1.3%, where LLVM's heuristics are already near-optimal for size), on functions from MediaBench and SPEC CPU2006. The authors report that running the generated code on Hexagon confirms that the estimated speedup becomes actual speedup.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are 'estimated' speedups from a static cost model, not measured runtimes, except for the Hexagon execution check. The metric is the quality of the generated code: Unison's constraint solving is far slower than LLVM's heuristic register allocator and scheduler, and the paper describes scaling to medium-sized functions of up to about 1,000 instructions, so compile time is a cost, not a win. The repo README and project site (unison-code.github.io index.md, checked via raw.githubusercontent.com) make no performance claims and link no results; the paper (arXiv 1804.02452, TOPLAS doi 10.1145/3332373), the project site's publication pages and the Ericsson research blog 'Outperforming state-of-the-art compilers with Unison' were unreachable here, so all numbers are from search-result text. Needs an LLVM fork (unison-code/llvm) as a driver. Last commit 2023-01-15 (abandoned). Filed under assemblers-and-asm-tooling, though it is really a compiler back-end component (register allocation and instruction scheduling).

notes: Real, peer-reviewed project; downgraded B to C only because the paper could not be opened here (arXiv, doi.org, deepai.org, ericsson.com all ENOTFOUND). Add to the paper-access retier list: arXiv 1804.02452 / TOPLAS 2019 would support B. Shortcomings: estimated (cost-model) speedups except on Hexagon, gains of 1.1-10% are small, much slower compile times than LLVM, abandoned since 2023-01-15.
